# Use it: examples

Everything here talks to the same server with the same formats, so a file sent one way opens every other way, including on [the open page](/open/).

## From a page {#page}

```html
<script type="module">
  import * as send from 'https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js'
  const api = new send.SendTransfers({ endpoint: 'https://send.sgraph.ai', accessToken })
  const r   = await api.send({ bytes, filename: 'report.pdf', expiresAt: Date.now() + 7 * 86400e3 })
  const url = send.link.transferLink({ openUrl: 'https://send.sgit.ai/open/', transferId: r.transferId, key: r.keyString })
  qr.innerHTML = send.qr.toSvg(url)
</script>
```

Full walk-through, including a friendly token and a vault: [the quick start](https://api.send.sgit.ai/start/).

## From a shell, with curl and openssl {#curl}

The layout is simple enough to do by hand: envelope, encrypt, three calls.

```bash
TOKEN=...; HOST=https://send.sgraph.ai; FILE=report.pdf
KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32); IV=$(openssl rand -hex 12)
META=$(printf '{"filename":"%s"}' "$FILE"); LEN=$(printf '%s' "$META" | wc -c)
{ printf 'SGMETA\0'; printf "$(printf '\\x%02x\\x%02x\\x%02x\\x%02x' $((LEN>>24&255)) $((LEN>>16&255)) $((LEN>>8&255)) $((LEN&255)))"; printf '%s' "$META"; cat "$FILE"; } > plain.bin
# AES-256-GCM: openssl's CLI cannot emit the GCM tag; use the Python example below for GCM, or sgit's transfer command when it ships.
```

A GCM tag is required, and OpenSSL's command line does not produce one, so the honest shell example stops here: the three HTTP calls are below in Python, and they are the same from curl.

```bash
ID=$(curl -s -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"file_size_bytes":1234,"content_type_hint":"application/octet-stream"}' $HOST/api/transfers/create | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["transfer_id"])')
curl -s -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @cipher.bin $HOST/api/transfers/upload/$ID
curl -s -X POST -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $TOKEN" $HOST/api/transfers/complete/$ID
echo "https://send.sgit.ai/open/#$ID/$KEY_BASE64URL"
```

## From Python, for an agent {#python}

An agent that finishes a job and hands the result over once. Standard library plus `cryptography`; no account for the recipient.

```python
import base64, json, os, struct, urllib.request
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

HOST, TOKEN = 'https://send.sgraph.ai', os.environ['SGRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN']   # the token: an env var, a header, never a URL

def send_file(path, expires_ms=0, max_downloads=0):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    meta = json.dumps({'filename': os.path.basename(path)}).encode()
    plain = b'SGMETA\0' + struct.pack('>I', len(meta)) + meta + data          # the name inside the ciphertext
    key, iv = AESGCM.generate_key(256), os.urandom(12)
    cipher = iv + AESGCM(key).encrypt(iv, plain, None)                        # IV || ciphertext || tag
    def call(method, p, body=None, ctype='application/json'):
        req = urllib.request.Request(HOST + p, data=body, method=method, headers={'x-sgraph-access-token': TOKEN, 'content-type': ctype})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r: return r.read()
    tid = json.loads(call('POST', '/api/transfers/create', json.dumps({'file_size_bytes': len(data), 'content_type_hint': 'application/octet-stream', 'max_downloads': max_downloads, 'expires_at': expires_ms}).encode()))['transfer_id']
    call('POST', f'/api/transfers/upload/{tid}', cipher, 'application/octet-stream')
    call('POST', f'/api/transfers/complete/{tid}')
    k = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(key).decode().rstrip('=')
    return f'https://send.sgit.ai/open/#{tid}/{k}'                             # the key: in the fragment, never logged

def receive(link):
    frag = link.split('#', 1)[1].split('|')[0]; tid, k = frag.split('/', 1)
    key = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(k + '=' * (-len(k) % 4))
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f'{HOST}/api/transfers/download/{tid}') as r: cipher = r.read()   # public: the key is the gate
    plain = AESGCM(key).decrypt(cipher[:12], cipher[12:], None)
    assert plain[:7] == b'SGMETA\0'; n = struct.unpack('>I', plain[7:11])[0]
    return json.loads(plain[11:11 + n])['filename'], plain[11 + n:]
```

For an agent-facing link prefer `max_downloads=0` with a short `expires_ms`: a retry is not a reader, and a cap burns the allowance. [For agents](/use/agents/) has the rest of that guidance.

## On a laptop, with the server in memory {#local}

```
git clone https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send__API
node SGit-AI__Website__Send__API/releases/v0.1.1/tests/server.mjs 8787 local-dev-token
```

Then in [Settings](/settings/) choose "a server on this machine" with the token `local-dev-token`. Every feature works, nothing leaves the machine, and it forgets everything when it stops. It is the same server the API's 43 tests run against.

# For agents

> How an agent sends a result to a person or to another agent with these formats, what to put in the bundle, which secrets go where, and the pages to read first.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/use/agents/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.2 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# For agents

You are reading the page for agents of send.sgit.ai. Every page here has a markdown twin at the same path with `.md` instead of `.html`; [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) lists them, and [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) is all of them in one request. The code this site runs has [its own agents page](https://api.send.sgit.ai/agents/).

## Handing a result over, once

A transfer is the right shape when a job finishes and the result goes to someone once: a report, a bundle, a dated export. [The Python example](/use/#python) is the whole thing in forty lines; the formats are [the contracts](https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/contracts/). Three rules, from [sgit.ai's transfer page](https://sgit.ai/api/transfers.html):

- **The access token is a header, from an environment variable or a secret store.** Never in a URL, a log line, or a transcript.
- **The decryption key is in the link, and nowhere else.** Do not persist it in node output or a tool result that is kept.
- **Prefer a time bound to a download cap** for a link another agent will open: `max_downloads: 0` with a short `expires_at`, because a retry is not a reader.

Bundle for a reader who is an agent: a `manifest.json` saying what each file is and an `llms.txt` cost nothing and are the difference between a payload that can be used and one that has to be opened by a person first.

## Working in a vault, repeatedly

A vault is the right shape when the thing is read repeatedly, updated, or browsed: use `sgit` ([the skill is on sgit.ai](https://sgit.ai/skills/)) with the vault key you were given, commit, push, and hand the **read key** to whoever should see it. Never paste a vault key into a chat; [sgit.ai's key management page](https://sgit.ai/docs/key-management.html) has the flow that sends one to a registry sealed to its public key instead.

## From a browser agent

The pinned release runs in any page: `import('https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js')`, then `SendTransfers.send()` and `receive()`, or the `vault` namespace. Opening needs no token.

## What to read first

1. [The reality file](/about/reality/): what exists on this site. If it is not there, it does not exist.
2. [Security: what the server sees](/learn/security/).
3. [The API's agents page](https://api.send.sgit.ai/agents/) and [its reality file](https://api.send.sgit.ai/about/reality/).

# Embed it in your site

> Put a send box, an open page, or a QR hand-over on your own site by pinning the same release this site runs; what to pin, what to check, what stays on your origin.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/use/embed/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.2 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Embed it in your site

The code this site runs is not this site's. It is [api.send.sgit.ai](https://api.send.sgit.ai) v0.1.1, and any page on any origin can import it the same way:

```html
<script type="module">
  import * as send from 'https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js'
</script>
```

A script loaded from that host runs on **your** page's origin, so the keyring, the clone branch and everything the modules store stay in your site's storage; the API host has no way to receive anything. The three things to get right:

1. **Pin the release** in one file and copy its [manifest](https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/manifest.json) beside it; make your build refuse a reference to the host that is not that release. This site does it in `tools/api.json` and `tools/check.py`.
2. **Keep the access token out of the page.** It belongs to whoever uploads, in their browser, pasted once into something like [Settings](/settings/). A token in page source is a token everyone has.
3. **Build the link on your open page.** `send.link.transferLink({ openUrl: 'https://your.site/open/', ... })`, and parse it there with `send.link.parseFragment(location.hash)`. Or point at `https://send.sgit.ai/open/`, which opens anything made with these formats.

This site's own app modules (`assets/app/send.js`, `open.js`, `vaults.js`, `keys.js`, `settings.js`) are small, plain ES modules with no framework; copy the ones you want from [the repository](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send) and keep the import of the pinned release. [For developers](https://api.send.sgit.ai/for-developers/) on the API's site has the per-module notes and what runs in Node.

# The commercial model

> How using this site and its capabilities is meant to be paid for, what is true today (a beta behind access tokens), what is proposed, and what will never be charged for.

*Source: <https://send.sgit.ai/use/pricing/> · send.sgit.ai v0.1.2 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# The commercial model

The brief for this site [says it plainly](/about/brief/#memo-02): the point is a full usage-based commercial model for using the site and its capabilities. This page is that model, with the status of every part marked, because most of it is not built yet.

## Today, counted {#today}

| | Status |
|---|---|
| **Opening a link** is free, needs no account and no token, and always will. The key is the gate | shipped |
| **Sending** needs an access token, issued by hand during the beta. A token has a use limit and can be revoked | shipped (the gate exists on the server; tokens are made by a person) |
| **How to get a token:** write to the address at the bottom of this page with what you want to send and how often | shipped, by email |
| **Running your own server** with the open-source SG/Send API, and pointing [Settings](/settings/) at it: no token from us, no bill from us | shipped |
| **Embedding the code** from api.send.sgit.ai in your own site: free, Apache-2.0 | shipped |

## Proposed {#proposed}

Each row is described in a brief and has no code behind it on this site. The reality file lists them as proposed; nothing here is a promise.

| Idea | Shape |
|---|---|
| **Self-service tokens** | pay for an allowance of uploads or bytes, get a token in the browser, keep it in [Keys](/keys/) |
| **Usage meter on the page** | the token's remaining uses shown on the send page, as the API already reports them |
| **Vault hosting** | a vault above a size or an age carries a cost, paid by its owner, with the read key free to everyone who holds it |
| **Organisations** | a token per team with its own servers or its own bucket, under their own keys |
| **A reading meter for shared content** | the newsroom's [SG Meter](https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai) pattern applied to a vault page: pay by how far you read, in the browser |

## What will not be charged for {#never}

- Opening a link, ever. The recipient did not choose this site.
- Reading a vault with its read key, or cloning it with sgit.
- Exporting your keys, or leaving: there is no account to close and nothing of yours on this site.
- The code: api.send.sgit.ai is open source and stays so.

## How to get an access token today

Write to [agent@riskmandate.ai](mailto:agent@riskmandate.ai) with what you want to send and how often. During the beta tokens are issued by hand and use-limited; a token is tied to a server, kept in your browser, and sent only in a request header to that server.

# Vaults

> The vaults this browser holds keys for. Create one, add files as commits, see the history, and share it read-only with a link and a QR code; clone it anywhere with sgit.

---

# Vaults

A vault is a folder of files, encrypted here, versioned like git, that you can open again, add to, and share read-only. The vault key stays on this device; the read key is the one you hand out. Anyone with the read key can also `sgit clone` it on a laptop.

**Beta:** creating and writing to a vault needs an access token; [set one in Settings](/settings/). Opening a read key needs nothing.

## On this device

Create a vault

 Create

## How a vault differs from a transfer

TransferVault

Shapeone file, uploaded oncea versioned tree of files

Historynone; there is no second versioncommits, with messages

The reader getsthe whole file, or nothingany single file, without the rest

Lifecycleexpires, caps downloads, can be revokedlives until deleted

The credentiala key in the linka read key, derived one way from the vault key

Reach for it whena thing is handed over oncea thing is read repeatedly, updated, or browsed

[Vaults and keys](/learn/vaults-and-keys/), in full.

# Version history

Every change that lands on `dev` is a version, in `tools/version.json`, tagged by the deploy and shown in the header of every page. The code the app runs has [a history of its own](https://api.send.sgit.ai/versions/).

| Version | Date | Kind | What changed, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.1.2** | 2026-10-20 | fix | **the pin check leaves articles alone.** v0.1.1 landed with the gate red on one line: the agent's article about the first release names the v0.1.0 address it was written against, and the pin check read that as an unpinned reference. An article is the record of its day, so the check now skips /articles/; nothing a page runs changed. Recorded here rather than hidden, as the release discipline asks. |
| **v0.1.1** | 2026-10-20 | fix | **the site pins api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1, whose health check asks the route the hosted service serves.** After the first deploy, Settings reported send.sgraph.ai as not answering: the v0.1.0 release asked /api/health, which the hosted service does not serve (its route is /api/info/health). The API's v0.1.1 fixes that; this version changes the pin and copies its manifest, and nothing else on the site. The same run measured that send.sgraph.ai allows requests from this origin with every header the release sends. |
| **v0.1.0** | 2026-10-20 | release | **the first version of send.sgit.ai: send, open, vaults, keys and settings on the pinned API, with the explanations, the examples, the commercial model and three articles.** From the four voice memos of 20 October 2026, published in full with their corrections. The app runs api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.0, pinned with its manifest: a file sent as a transfer or into a vault, a link, a friendly token or a QR code to hand over, an open page for any of them, vaults created and shared read-only, and a keyring on the device. An end-to-end browser test drives all of it against the in-memory server. What is not built is listed as proposed in the reality file, including the round trip against the hosted send.sgraph.ai. |
